title: #oratorioforlivingthings #heatherchristian #signaturetheatre #theatre...
transcript: Okay, this was one of my most anticipated shows for the Fall, and for good reason. Oratorio For Living Things by Heather Christian is a strange and beautiful musical exploration of time on three scales — the quantum, the human, and the cosmic. You don't really have to know what this means to have a transformative experience. Almost entirely sung through, this piece feels like a blend of choral music, gospel, jazz, and soul, exquisitely brought to life by a dozen vocalists and a band. The composition itself and the vocal arrangements are so intricate and dense, and the way the room is set up makes it super immersive — you literally feel like you're inside the music. The moments of high dynamic contrast are striking, and I thought the vocal blend was astonishing. For all the strengths this piece has, I didn't find it to be a physically comfortable experience. Being in the front row, I had to do a lot of head turning, and I was constantly worried that a performer was going to trip over me. The trade off, though, was the proximity to the performers and getting a perfectly calibrated audio mix from the center of the room — one that I think you would never be able to capture on a cast recording. Overall, I found this more intellectually stimulating than emotionally impactful, but it was really impressive and unlike anything I've ever seen. I do think it's a must see, especially if you're into choral or gospel music. Oratorio For Living Things is running at Signature into mid-November. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: First-hand attendance confirmed (sat front row, describes physical discomfort from head-turning). Creator gives detailed opinions on composition, vocal blend, and immersive setup of Heather Christian's piece at Signature Theatre.
